organism_context: Burkholderia sp. HME13 and other ergothioneine-utilising bacteria, including human gut anaerobes; homotetramer of identical 55 kDa subunits, distantly related to histidine/phenylalanine ammonia-lyase
rationale: KEGG R04877 is annotated 'ergothionase'; the purified Burkholderia HME13 enzyme is a single-activity C-N lyase that eliminates trimethylamine from ergothioneine and was inactive on D/L-histidine, tyrosine and phenylalanine. No second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Ergothionase is purely catabolic (ergothioneine is instead synthesised by the unrelated EgtA-EgtE route), so the physiological flux is ergothioneine -> trimethylamine + thiourocanate, i.e. the LLM's '>' rather than ModelSEED's '<'.

organism_context: Phosphonolipid-producing eukaryotes (Tetrahymena, molluscs) and bacteria; no protein assigned
rationale: KEGG flags R04925 as an 'incomplete reaction (methylation)' with no EC number and no ortholog, and literature searches returned no characterised methylaminoethylphosphonate N-methyltransferase; the catalysing protein is simply not known.
direction_note: The underlying biology is a SAM-dependent N-methylation (monomethyl -> dimethyl aminoethylphosphonate), which is biosynthetically one-way and corresponds to the LLM's '>'; the ModelSEED equation omits SAM/SAH, so its thermodynamic direction call is not meaningful.

organism_context: Selenium-accumulating plants (Allium, Brassica) by analogy with the sulfur alk(en)ylcysteine sulfoxide pathway; no protein assigned
rationale: KEGG marks R04934 as an 'incomplete reaction' with no EC, no ortholog and no pathway, and it lumps Se-alkylation plus Se-oxidation into one step; no enzyme catalysing it has been reported.
direction_note: In Se-accumulating plants the biosynthetic flux runs from selenocysteine toward Se-alkyl-selenocysteine Se-oxides, which favours the LLM's '>', but this is a lumped multi-step stub rather than a reversible single-enzyme reaction.

enzyme_name: Enterobactin synthetase (EntF non-ribosomal peptide synthetase, acting with EntE and EntB)
distinct_activities: amide-bond condensation of 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl onto seryl-S-PCP (C domain)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other Enterobacteriaceae; EntF is a 142 kDa four-domain (C-A-PCP-TE) single polypeptide
rationale: The chain that builds enterobactin from the two adenylates is EntF, one 142 kDa polypeptide carrying condensation, adenylation, carrier and thioesterase domains (three genuine catalytic activities plus a carrier). Its partner EntB is separately a fused bifunctional isochorismatase-aryl carrier protein; the overall reaction is run by a three-protein assembly line (EntB/EntE/EntF), not a single enzyme.
direction_note: NRPS assembly-line chemistry is driven by ATP-derived aminoacyl/aryl-adenylates and terminated by irreversible TE-catalysed trilactonisation, so the step is physiologically unidirectional toward enterobactin ('>'), never back to the adenylates.

organism_context: Coumarin-producing plants (e.g. Melilotus, Hierochloe) and generic glycoside hydrolase family 1 beta-glucosidases (KEGG K01188/K05349/K05350)
rationale: KEGG R04998 is assigned only to generic GH1 beta-glucosidases, which are single-active-site retaining glycoside hydrolases with no second catalytic activity; the specific protein hydrolysing the 2-coumarinate glucoside has not been individually purified, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: Glycosidases operate hydrolytically in vivo and the released cis-2-coumarate is immediately pulled off by spontaneous lactonisation to coumarin, so flux runs in the glucose-releasing direction ('>'); the glucoside is made by a UDP-glucosyltransferase, not by reversal of this enzyme.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous lactonisation of cis-2-coumarate to coumarin
organism_context: Plant coumarin biosynthesis (MetaCyc PWY-5176)
rationale: KEGG annotates R04999 explicitly as 'non enzymatic' and MetaCyc RXN-8037 is a spontaneous reaction; there is no catalysing protein, so no functionality class applies.
direction_note: Spontaneous intramolecular lactonisation of cis-2-coumarate to coumarin is effectively irreversible at physiological pH, so the real direction is the LLM's '>' (coumarin formation + water release).

organism_context: KEGG C5-branched dibasic acid metabolism (4-methyleneglutamate metabolism is documented in Arachis and some actinomycetes); no protein assigned
rationale: KEGG R05079 carries no EC number, no ortholog and no comment, and literature searches for 4-methylene-2-oxoglutarate / 4-methylglutamate enzymes returned nothing; the catalysing enzyme is unknown.
direction_note: The ModelSEED equation is redox-unbalanced (it converts a methylene oxo acid to a methyl amino acid with four bare protons and no reductant), so no enzymological argument can settle its direction.

organism_context: Granatane alkaloid biosynthesis in Punica granatum and related piperidine-alkaloid plants
rationale: KEGG annotates R05131 as an 'incomplete reaction' with the explicit note 'enzyme not yet characterized', and the granatane/tropane alkaloid literature still lists the pelletierine N-methylation step as having no identified protein.
direction_note: The step is a SAM-dependent N-methylation, which is biosynthetically one-way toward N-methylpelletierine, matching the LLM's '>'; the ModelSEED equation omits SAM/SAH so its direction call rests on bare skeleton thermodynamics.

organism_context: Escherichia coli, lactic acid bacteria and other PTS-using bacteria; glycoside hydrolase family 1 (KEGG K01222/K01223)
rationale: GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidases are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 glycosidases with one catalytic Glu pair and no second activity; structures of several human-microbiome GH1 6-P-beta-glucosidases confirm the single-active-site architecture.
direction_note: This is the intracellular hydrolytic step of PTS-coupled aryl-glucoside catabolism: the phospho-glucoside is cleaved irreversibly to glucose 6-phosphate plus aglycone ('>'), and the condensation direction ModelSEED prefers does not occur in vivo.

organism_context: Escherichia coli, lactic acid bacteria and other PTS-using bacteria; glycoside hydrolase family 1 (KEGG K01222/K01223)
rationale: Same GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidases as for arbutin 6-phosphate (EC 3.2.1.86); these are single-active-site retaining glycosidases, with substrate breadth across salicin/arbutin/cellobiose phosphates rather than a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of salicin 6-phosphate to glucose 6-phosphate plus saligenin is the catabolic, irreversible direction ('>'); glucoside synthesis from G6P is not a physiological reverse of this enzyme.

organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF1293 (bialaphos biosynthesis); 32.7 kDa single-domain protein of the PEP-mutase/isocitrate-lyase superfamily (KEGG K12909)
rationale: The purified and overexpressed enzyme is a single ~295-residue polypeptide; mechanistic work shows the decarboxylation proceeds through an enzyme-bound carboxyphosphinopyruvate intermediate within the one active site, so the rearrangement-plus-decarboxylation is one catalytic activity with a two-step mechanism, not two fused activities.
direction_note: Loss of CO2 from the rearranged intermediate makes the step effectively irreversible toward (hydroxyphosphinyl)pyruvate, i.e. the LLM's '>'; a phosphonomutase running backwards against CO2 release is not physiological.

organism_context: Benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid plants, notably Coptis japonica and Papaver somniferum (KEGG K13384)
rationale: The enzyme is a single-domain class-II SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase; its two EC listings (2.1.1.115 and 2.1.1.140) reflect substrate promiscuity across 1-benzyl-tetrahydroisoquinolines, not two distinct catalytic chemistries.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer with SAH release is biosynthetically unidirectional toward reticuline ('>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require remethylating SAH, which this enzyme does not do.

organism_context: Sacred lotus (Nelumbo nucifera), where R-enantiospecific N-methyltransferases drive the (R)-BIA pathway; KEGG K13384 / MetaCyc RXN-19908
rationale: The (R)-selective counterpart of CNMT identified in Nelumbo nucifera is a single-domain SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase; the only distinction from the (S)-enzyme is enantioselectivity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: As for the (S)-enzyme, SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer runs one way toward (R)-reticuline ('>'), so the enzymology supports the LLM call rather than ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: Hydrogenobyrinate a,c-diamide synthase (CobB; CbiA in the anaerobic pathway), EC 6.3.5.9
distinct_activities: glutamine amidotransferase / glutaminase (class I GATase domain, N-terminal)
ATP-dependent carboxylate amidoligase (synthetase domain, C-terminal; EC 6.3.5.9)
organism_context: Pseudomonas denitrificans (CobB, aerobic cobalamin pathway); CbiA in Salmonella enterica
rationale: CobB is a classic glutamine amidotransferase: one polypeptide carries an N-terminal class-I glutaminase domain that hydrolyses glutamine to glutamate + ammonia and a C-terminal ATP-dependent amidoligase domain (a dethiobiotin-synthetase-like fold) that amidates the a and c carboxylates. The two activities sit in separate active sites on the same chain, so this is a fused bifunctional enzyme rather than a complex.
direction_note: Both half-reactions are hydrolytic drivers (2 ATP -> ADP + Pi and glutamine -> glutamate), so amidation is strongly irreversible toward the diamide ('>'); ModelSEED's equation drops ADP and glutamate, so its '<' call is computed on a truncated, non-physiological stoichiometry.

organism_context: Nocardia (Amycolatopsis) lactamdurans and Streptomyces clavuligerus, cephamycin C cluster (KEGG K04128)
rationale: cmcH from both cephamycin producers encodes a single functional O-carbamoyltransferase that transfers carbamoyl from carbamoyl phosphate to the 3'-hydroxymethyl of deacetylcephalosporin C; no second catalytic activity is reported for the protein.
direction_note: Carbamoyl transfer releases inorganic phosphate from carbamoyl phosphate, a high-energy donor, making the biosynthetic direction ('>') effectively irreversible.

organism_context: DDT co-metabolism by biphenyl/PCB-degrading bacteria (Alcaligenes eutrophus A5, Pandoraea pnomenusa B-356, Comamonas testosteroni B-356); homotetrameric short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase
rationale: KEGG assigns R05395 only to 'cis-2,3-dihydrodiol DDT dehydrogenase', which in practice is the broad-specificity biphenyl dihydrodiol dehydrogenase BphB of the biphenyl pathway; BphB is a classical single-active-site SDR with one Ser-Tyr-Lys catalytic triad. The enzyme identity is inferred from pathway/substrate breadth, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: The dehydrogenase aromatises the cis-dihydrodiol to the catechol, a strongly downhill step that is pulled further by ring-cleavage dioxygenase; catabolic flux is therefore the oxidative direction ('>'), not NADH-driven re-reduction.

enzyme_name: cis-2,3-Dihydrodiol DDT dehydrogenase, NADP(+) form (biphenyl dihydrodiol dehydrogenase, BphB)
organism_context: Same enzyme/organisms as R05395; KEGG lists R05396 purely as the NADP(+) bookkeeping duplicate of R05395
rationale: R05396 is the same cis-2,3-dihydrodiol DDT dehydrogenase activity written with NADP(+) (KEGG cross-references the two entries); BphB-type SDRs are single-activity enzymes and are in fact NAD(+)-preferring, so the NADP form is an annotation variant rather than a different protein.
direction_note: As for the NAD form, the physiological flux is dihydrodiol -> catechol oxidation ('>'), driven forward by the downstream ring-cleavage step.

organism_context: Chlorocatechol-degrading Proteobacteria (Ralstonia eutropha JMP134, Pseudomonas sp. P51, Pseudomonas putida) and Rhodococcus; Mg2+-dependent octameric enolase-superfamily enzyme
rationale: The modified ortho-cleavage clusters (clcABD, tfdCDEF, tcbCDEF) encode a dedicated chloromuconate cycloisomerase that both cyclises and eliminates chloride in a single active site; purified chloro/dichloromuconate cycloisomerases show only cycloisomerase activity, with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: Cycloisomerisation of 2,4-dichloromuconate is accompanied by chloride elimination, which makes the step effectively irreversible toward the chlorodienelactone ('>').

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain P51 chlorobenzene pathway (tcbAB); NAD(+)-dependent short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase, KEGG K16269
rationale: KEGG names the catalysing protein TcbB, a cis-dihydrodiol dehydrogenase of the same SDR family as BphB; these are single-active-site NAD-dependent dehydrogenases with no second catalytic activity. Identity is from the KEGG/MetaCyc assignment rather than a dedicated TcbB biochemistry paper, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: Aromatisation of the chlorinated cis-dihydrodiol to 3,6-dichlorocatechol is the catabolic, essentially irreversible direction ('>'), pulled by the downstream chlorocatechol dioxygenase.

organism_context: Aromatoleum aromaticum EbN1, anaerobic ethylbenzene degradation; a heterooligomeric Apc(aa'bg)2 core complex of 482 kDa plus a separate 34 kDa Apc-epsilon subunit
rationale: Acetophenone carboxylase is a multi-subunit complex of separate polypeptides (an ATP-hydrolysing module and a carboxylating module on distinct chains), which per the exclusion rule is not a fused bifunctional enzyme; the single carboxylation activity is the honest call.
direction_note: The real reaction consumes 2 ATP -> 2 ADP + 2 Pi to drive carboxylation, making it irreversible toward benzoylacetate ('>'); ModelSEED's equation drops the ATP entirely, so its '<' call is computed for a bare CO2 addition rather than the ATP-driven reaction, which is the likely source of the disagreement.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous lactonisation of 2-succinylbenzoyl-CoA to the spirodilactone
organism_context: Menaquinone (ubiquinone and other terpenoid-quinone) biosynthesis, KEGG rn00130
rationale: KEGG annotates R05455 with the single comment 'spontaneous' and assigns no EC number or ortholog; the step is a non-enzymatic intramolecular cyclisation that diverts SB-CoA, so there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: A spontaneous, CoA-releasing intramolecular lactonisation runs only toward the spirodilactone ('>'); it is a chemical dead-end side reaction, not a reversible enzymatic step.

enzyme_name: unidentified (nearest real chemistry: oxytetracycline tailoring by OxyS hydroxylase / OxyR dehydrotetracycline reductase)
organism_context: Oxytetracycline biosynthesis in Streptomyces rimosus (oxy/otc cluster)
rationale: The source reaction KEGG R05461 has been withdrawn (the REST entry now 404s), and the retained ModelSEED stoichiometry is a bare hydration of 12-dehydrotetracycline with no O2 or NAD(P)H, which matches no characterised enzyme; the real terminal tailoring steps (OxyS C-hydroxylation, OxyR/dehydrotetracycline reductase) have different stoichiometries.
direction_note: If the entry stands in for terminal oxytetracycline tailoring, pathway flux is toward oxytetracycline ('>'), but the lumped equation omits the O2/NAD(P)H couple that actually makes that direction irreversible, so neither direction call rests on real enzymology.

organism_context: Streptomyces clavuligerus clavulanic acid cluster; NADPH-dependent short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase catalysing the final pathway step
rationale: The terminal step of clavulanic acid biosynthesis is the NADPH-dependent reduction of clavaldehyde (clavulanate-9-aldehyde) to clavulanic acid by the cad-encoded SDR, a single-activity oxidoreductase; the ModelSEED reaction omits NADPH, so the enzyme assignment is by pathway position, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: CAD runs reductively in vivo (clavaldehyde -> clavulanate, the pathway's committed last step), matching the LLM's '>'; because ModelSEED strips the NADPH out, its '<' call is based on bare proton stoichiometry rather than on the real NADPH-driven reduction.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG-lumped multi-step segment of the DDT meta-cleavage route
organism_context: Aerobic DDT co-metabolism by biphenyl-pathway bacteria (KEGG rn00351)
rationale: KEGG annotates R05472 with the comment 'multi-step reaction' and assigns no EC number or ortholog; it compresses hydrolysis of the ring-fission product to 4-chlorobenzoate into a single entry, so no individual catalysing enzyme exists to classify.
direction_note: As a lumped degradative segment, flux runs catabolically toward 4-chlorobenzoate ('>'); it is not a reversible single-enzyme step in either direction.

organism_context: Co-metabolic DDT transformation by diphenylmethane/benzhydrol-grown bacteria and by white-rot fungi (Phanerochaete chrysosporium)
rationale: KEGG R05479 carries no EC number, ortholog or comment, and the DDA -> DBP conversion is only reported as a co-metabolic transformation in whole-cell and fungal studies; no protein has been purified for it.
direction_note: The step is an oxidative-decarboxylative degradation toward DBP ('>'), a direction set by the catabolic route rather than by any reversible enzyme.
